## Retro Cyberpunk & The Mega Man Anomaly

A vibrant wave of nostalgia is sweeping through the *Pepermint Comic* and PC-9801 enthusiast communities. The cluster centers on high-resolution scans of 1980s Japanese visual media, specifically highlighting the work of artist Takeshi Akabishiwa. Fans are buzzing over distinct retro-cyberpunk aesthetics, from neon-lit mech designs to character art featuring blue-haired motorcyclists and pink-haired fantasy warriors.

One standout anecdote involves *Rockman Neo*, a *Mega Man* project where a rough "dummy" title screen was so charmingly effective that it was accidentally elevated to official status due to tight deadlines. This accidental preservation has sparked detailed analyses of the era’s unique artistic license, bridging the gap between manga, mecha anime, and early hardware constraints.

## Hardware Wars: 3D Prints, Polls, and Nikon Rumors

The /gg/ gear boards are alive with technical debate. In one thread, users dissect a 3D-printed camera grip made of ABS plastic. Opinions are split: some mock it as compensation for small sensors, while others praise the engineering required to handle bending moments, noting that plastic often fails where metal succeeds. Meta-commentary here also touches on the unreliability of AI reverse image searching, citing the "Trevor Wisecup" incident as proof of "deuterated bullshit."

Simultaneously, a poll designed to filter bots has become a battleground. Accusations fly between users "Oly anon" and the community, with claims of VPN-based vote manipulation versus organic backlash. Meanwhile, rumors swirl around Nikon’s potential Z5IIC. This compact, full-frame rangefinder-style camera is expected to compete directly with Sony’s a7c series. While some see hope in a non-Sony compact option, skeptics dismiss it as a "painted plastic" refresh utilizing an eight-year-old sensor and the aging Expeed 7 processor.

## AI Engineering Goes Industrial

The conversation around AI is shifting from experimental hype to production maturity. InfoQ’s QCon AI New York 2026, scheduled for December, promises to address the "industrial revolution" of enterprise adoption. Key sessions will cover agent authorization, production guardrails, and shared inference infrastructure.

Technical deep dives, particularly around the "Agent Harness" article, are comparing implementation strategies for finance assistants. The debate centers on AWS AgentCore versus LangChain with Envoy AI Gateway, evaluating trade-offs in tool handling, memory management, and cost control. This signals a broader industry trend toward open-source sovereignty and reliability over mere novelty.

## Music Production: Digital Broadcast vs. Analog Tactility

Music producers are showcasing two distinct philosophies on Mastodon. On one end, @bandog- presents a high-end PC-centric DJ station. The setup features Pioneer CDJ-3000s, Technics turntables, and a laptop running "THUNDERDOME," all bathed in vibrant purple and blue ambient lighting, emphasizing broadcast aesthetics and hybrid vinyl-digital performance.

Contrasting this is @OkDate3120’s "Final live performance setup." Eschewing a DAW entirely, this rig relies on tactile hardware: an Akai MPC, Eurorack modules, an Arturia Keystep Pro, and a Moog Mother-32. Operating in a studio with a sloped ceiling, the user highlights a return to manual knob-turning and pad triggering, proving that standalone analog and digital synthesizers still hold significant appeal for live execution.

## COSMIC Epoch 1.9: Rust-Powered Linux Updates

System76 has made significant strides in its open-source desktop environment with the release of COSMIC Epoch 1.9. The update introduces two native Rust-based applications: COSMIC Viewer, the new default image viewer with built-in editing, and the COSMIC OSK on-screen keyboard, which supports touchscreen and gamepad input. The release also features a redesigned Store displaying developer names and improvements to the compositor, marking a key milestone for the Rust-centric Linux project.

## Local Weather & Events

In San Diego, the NWS bot reports above-normal temperatures, with coastal areas running up to 10 degrees higher than average. While humidity is rising, cloud cover keeps the heat moderate. Meanwhile, local event bots are promoting guitarist Geoff Nigl’s acoustic performance at Galpao Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse on September 27, 2026.

## Quick Hits

*   **Vintage VW Love:** @bitemywire shared a stunning shot of a vintage Volkswagen Type 2 bus (T2) using a Takumar 50mm lens on a Canon 5Dmk3, praising the analog aesthetic.
*   **Pokémon Fan Art:** A hand-drawn illustration of Oshawott holding a pamphlet that reads "I ALL ABOUT" is circulating, noted for its soft, cartoon style and cute expressive design.
*   **Singapore vs. Korea:** 4chan’s /trv/ board is settling a debate, with South Korea’s winter hiking and village experiences currently beating Singapore’s "small" snow facilities and "third world" dating scene.

@台羽正 (tadashidaiba.bsky.social) —  This is a colorful manga-style illustration depicting a video game development scene, likely related to the *Mega Man* franchise. **Main Characters:** - On the left stands a young man with spiky red hair and a wide grin. He wears a blue armored bodysuit resembling Mega Man’s design, with a high collar, shoulder pads, and gauntlets. A speech bubble next to him reads “ガビーン” (Gabin), an exclamation of surprise. - On the right sits an older man with white hair, a long white beard, round glasses, and a red robe — clearly Professor Light (Dr. Light) from Mega Man. He appears stressed or exhausted, sitting in a chair with his hands on his knees. A pink thought bubble above him contains the text: “これやな、ひどいのう…” (“This is terrible…”). **Central Object:** Between them is a large, brown, chalkboard-like screen displaying what looks like a prototype title screen for a game: - Top line: “ロックマンネオ” (Rockman Neo) - Middle: “~国地妻 危機一発!!~” (~National Wife Crisis Moment!!~) — “国地妻” (Kunuchi Tsuma) literally means “National Wife,” possibly a placeholder or inside joke. - Bottom: “サブタイトル PRESS START” (Subtitle PRESS START) **Background & Decorations:** - The background features abstract green and purple brush strokes. - At the top, bold yellow starburst text says: “キング オブ 仮キャラ” (“King of Dummy Characters”) - Below that: “いなかまん最早つくられたタイトル画面” (“Early Title Screen Created by Inaka-man”) - Credits: “BY マッゴー（ソフトマン）” — “Made by Magoo (Softman)” - Side credits near the red-haired character: “B.Y. しば裏” — possibly a pseudonym or team name. **Narrative Text at Bottom:** A paragraph of Japanese text explains the story behind this title screen: > “It was used for about 2–3 months into the initial phase!! ... But one day, unexpectedly, customers came to see ‘Neo’. ‘Since the national wife is bad, can you make something presentable for customers by tomorrow?’ ... At that time, the clock was approaching 2 AM. ... And this thing we made in just one hour ended up being used for over a year.” The tone is humorous and nostalgic, celebrating the makeshift nature of early game development. --- **Translation Summary (Japanese to English):** Title/Header: - “King of Dummy Characters” - “Early Title Screen Created by Inaka-man” - “By Magoo (Softman)” On-screen game title: - “Rockman Neo” - “~National Wife Crisis Moment!!~” - “Subtitle PRESS START” Speech bubbles: - Red-haired character: “Gabin!” (surprised yell) - Dr. Light: “This is terrible…” Bottom narrative: Explains that this rough title screen was originally intended only for internal use during the first 2–3 months of development. When external clients arrived to view the project, they were asked to create a presentable version by the next day. With only one hour before the deadline (approaching 2 AM), they made this version — which ironically became the official title screen for over a year. --- This image captures a lighthearted, behind-the-scenes anecdote from game development, blending humor with affection for retro gaming culture.

clusters.summary: The cluster centers on vintage Japanese visual media from the 1980s, specifically covers and illustrations from the magazine *Pepermint Comic* (or *Be-Bermint Comic*) and related game art. Key entities include artist **Takeshi Akabishiwa** (also spelled Akashiima) and character designs featuring retro-cyberpunk aesthetics, such as a blue-haired woman with a motorcycle and a pink-haired fantasy warrior from the PC-9801 game *Mahjong Fantasia III*. One notable post highlights a humorous behind-the-scenes anecdote about a rough "dummy" title screen for a *Mega Man* project called *Rockman Neo*, which inadvertently became official due to a tight deadline. Users are sharing high-resolution scans and detailed descriptions of these artifacts, noting specific stylistic elements like neon color palettes, mech designs, and the distinct anime art style of the era. The collection collectively celebrates the nostalgia of early 80s Japanese pop culture, bridging manga, mecha anime, and early video game development.

representative_texts: @Kagi News - Linux & OSS — System76 releases COSMIC 1.9 desktop with viewer, keyboard — System76 released COSMIC Epoch 1.9 on September 24, adding two native applications to its Rust-based Linux desktop: COSMIC Viewer for images and COSMIC OSK, an on-screen keyboard. The release also updates the compositor and existing desktop apps. System76 recommends COSMIC Viewer as the desktop’s default image viewer. COSMIC OSK supports touchscreen and gamepad input and can be enabled through a panel applet; it can also appear on the lock screen. Highlights: Image editing: COSMIC Viewer supports a range of image formats and includes built-in editing features. Store redesign: The redesigned COSMIC Store displays developer names directly on application cards. Sources: COSMIC 1.9 Desktop Environment Released with COSMIC Viewer and COSMIC OSK - 9to5linux.com COSMIC Desktop 1.9 Adds COSMIC Viewer, On-Screen Keyboard - linuxiac.com COSMIC Epoch 1.9 Brings New Image Viewer & On-Screen Keyboard - phoronix.com
clusters.summary: System76 released COSMIC Epoch 1.9 on September 24, introducing two new native Rust-based applications to its Linux desktop environment: COSMIC Viewer and the COSMIC OSK on-screen keyboard. COSMIC Viewer, recommended as the default image viewer, supports various formats and includes built-in editing features, while the OSK accommodates touchscreen and gamepad input and can appear on the lock screen. The update also features a redesigned COSMIC Store that displays developer names on application cards and improvements to the compositor. Coverage from sources like 9to5linux, Linuxiac, and Phoronix highlights these additions as key milestones for the open-source desktop project.
